draft:
# Recover a paused Glassreed sweep

## Purpose and entry conditions

Use this runbook when a greenhouse imaging sweep has stopped before its planned frames were accepted. A sweep belongs to one greenhouse and one scheduled capture slot. Keep that identity visible while working: recovery continues the original sweep ID rather than turning the remaining work into a separate sweep. This makes the completion decision refer to the original capture plan.

Recovery appends missing frames to the original sweep. It never overwrites frames that the sweep has already accepted. An interrupted recovery therefore does not require replacing the accepted part of the capture.

Only a sweep in the **paused** state can be resumed. Inspection is also available for shadow greenhouses, but recovery is unavailable there. Before opening a recovery job, confirm that the greenhouse is an operational target and that the displayed sweep is the capture slot you intend to finish.

## Inspect and request recovery

Open **Sweeps > Recovery** and inspect the sweep. Read `inspect.gaps` as the authoritative list of missing frames. Use that list to understand the unfinished work; a remembered frame count from a previous operator is not a substitute for the current gap list.

Request a recovery ticket for the greenhouse being handled. Each ticket is limited to one greenhouse and can create a job for 30 minutes after issuance. If a ticket has already created a recovery job, submitting it again returns that job. It does not schedule another copy of the recovery work. This is useful when a browser response disappears and the operator cannot tell whether the request reached the service.

Record the original sweep ID in the handoff so another operator can relate the job to the planned capture. The recovery should be assessed against the same sweep, not against an informal list of images that happen to be visible.

## Watch progress and decide when to intervene

An active recovery emits a heartbeat every 15 seconds. Treat the job as stalled after 90 seconds without a heartbeat. These intervals describe job liveness; the presence of a heartbeat does not by itself establish that every planned frame has arrived.

If you cancel the recovery, the accepted images remain available. Reinspect the missing-frame list before deciding what remains to be done. Completion requires acceptance of every planned frame, including frames that were missing before this recovery attempt began. A cancellation and a successful completion are consequently different outcomes even when most images are present.

## Resolve an uncertain submission

When an earlier submission may have succeeded, use its ticket to retrieve the existing recovery job. Repeating that submission refers back to the already-created work rather than adding a second job. Ticket expiration blocks creation of a new job, but lookup of an existing job remains available for 24 hours after ticket issuance. Do not mistake the shorter creation window for the lookup window.

## Close the handoff

Recovery appends missing frames to the original sweep. It never overwrites frames that the sweep has already accepted. An interrupted recovery therefore does not require replacing the accepted part of the capture.

State whether the sweep completed, remained paused, or had its recovery canceled. Include the original sweep ID and the observed gaps when work remains. The receiving operator should be able to connect the status to the original plan without reconstructing which capture slot the recovery concerned.
